findings.summary: Probe README/PR body overstated 'before': warm-802 row did not reproduce (296 vs 801 ms), warm 3.2k/10.8k 'before' rows were still curating, and the 1557 ms max was a single unreproduced sample. Warm 'before' table dropped, 1557 labelled, reviewer N=3 re-run added (f3e728f)
'Fixes #396' while the floor still scales linearly and the harness re-measure is unrun: now 'Refs #396'; follow-up #448 (f3e728f)
In-lock deadline re-check untested (B1 survived): test asserts no whole-brain read (f3e728f)
Meta write on the error path untested (B2 survived): mid-run write failure test (f3e728f)
Busy-lock skip indistinguishable from a deadline stop: stderr line added and asserted (f3e728f)
Repair loop has no per-entry deadline check (repairs are rare; archive loop and in-lock re-check bound the normal path)
writeMeta throwing in the finally masks the original error (session-end catches both; CLI message less informative)
PR body said 5 new tests; now 7

ruledOut: semantic equivalence of snapshot edits: snapshot entry equals what updateEntry's readAll would read; every same-id read-before-write path in src/ takes the lock; addEntry uses fresh ids
repair and archive cannot edit the same id in one run (repaired ids excluded)
decision-family guard still enforced in applyFluidEdit; journal still mirrors every record
lock opts: dead/stale holders still broken at timeout 0; negative timeout skips; non-deadlined callers keep the 5 s fail-open; re-entrant path unaffected
stderr line only reachable from session-end's deadlined autoCurate; hook stdout JSON untouched
after-fix timings reproduced by the reviewer (10.8k cold 534 ms vs README 507 ms)
no false positives: a busy lock previously waited 5 s then skipped via the in-lock check anyway
